messages:
marco.procure: FYI Vendor Z sent a pilot quote and an unusual clause about "credit stacking". They propose pilot credits that can be applied at renewal but only up to 50% of the first-year commit. Thoughts?

tara.finance: can you drop the quote here? curious how they calculate the 50%. if it's percent-of-commit we need clarity on baseline (list vs. discounted commit).

marco.procure: attached snippet they emailed:
```
Pilot Credit: $15k applied to invoices during pilot. At renewal, up to 50% of annual committed invoice amount may be offset by unused pilot credits, subject to vendor audit. Credits expire 12 months from issuance.
```
they also have a line: "credits do not reduce minimum commit tiers" which is vague.

lucas.sales: that last part kills our goal to count credits toward meeting the threshold for a discount tier. We usually ask that pilot credits count against committed spend for the first contract year and for tier eligibility.

anya.billing: operational issue: if credits are applied at renewal they change invoicing. Need clear runbook: will vendor create a credit memo applied to month 1 of the contract? Also, tax/VAT treatment depends on whether credits are treated as discount vs. post-invoice rebate. We should get our tax counsel involved if material.

tara.finance: good call. From our economics POV: two acceptable variants: A) Credits convert to dollar-for-dollar prepayment against the first 12 months of committed spend (reduces committed liability). B) Credits apply only as a one-time invoice reduction but not toward commit or tiering. We prefer A. If vendor resists, counter with a cap on the portion that counts for tiering (e.g., 75% of credits count).

marco.procure: vendor replied in thread: "We can allow conversion up to 50% toward year-1 commit but require an executed amendment and reserve the right to audit usage. Pilot invoices already paid are non-refundable."

lucas.sales: ask them to change to 75% and remove "non-refundable" wording for paid pilot fees if amendment is signed within 30 days. We can offer a shorter amendment window if needed.

anya.billing: if they remove non-refundable AND allow conversion, we need to document timing for revenue recognition. Also include a clause that credits cannot be double-counted against multiple invoices. Add: "Vendor will issue a single credit memo documenting conversion details."

tara.finance: also add an audit right to verify unused credits against pilot invoices and usage logs. And include a sunset: any converted credits applied within first billing cycle of year-1 or they revert. Keeps accounting clean.

marco.procure: other ask from security: vendor must provide SOC2 Type II or an attestation within 45 days for ingest >5k devices. If they can't, we limit scope to 2k devices for the pilot.

vendorbot: Vendor Z uploaded revised quote: https://vendorz.example.com/quote/2026-03-05 (v2)

lucas.sales: I'll push vendor for 75% conversion, 30-day amendment window, and removal of non-refundable sentence. If vendor pushes back on 75% we can accept 60% with SLA credits in play.

anya.billing: also request explicit invoice example showing pre- and post-conversion accounting entries. Makes it easier for our AP and tax teams.

tara.finance: sounds good. If we get 60% conversion + audit right + SOC2 attestation or reduced scope, we can approve pilot payment and mark for PO. Keep me posted; I'll prepare an internal memo for booking treatment.

marco.procure: thanks — i'll respond to vendor with: 1) ask for conversion language to be dollar-for-dollar prepayment against year-1 invoice and percent converted (we're requesting 75%); 2) require a credit memo and audit right; 3) SOC2 attestation or reduced scope; 4) sample invoice illustrating conversion and tax treatment. sending now. :email:

anya.billing: ping me once they send sample invoice, i'll triage with tax and AP.

marco.procure: will do. closing loop after vendor replies.
